title: Boundary Inference for Mixed Fractional Models under High-Frequency Observation Critical LAN and Score Tests at $H=3/4$
summary: We study boundary inference at $H=3/4$ for mixed fractional Brownian motion and mixed fractional Ornstein--Uhlenbeck models under high-frequency observation. This boundary is economically important because it separates the critical and supercritical regimes of mixed fractional dynamics. We make three contributions. First, we identify the exact critical first-order scaling and show that, after removing the explicit linear component in the $H$-score, the transformed $(σ,H)$ block is already non-degenerate.
